recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12442 unless a future work group decision intentionally changes Questionnaire answer-code binding policy.
issue_request: FHIR-12442 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU2 and asked that missing bindings on Questionnaire.item.enableWhen.answer[x] and Questionnaire.item.initial[x] be added, using an example SNOMED-based answer-code binding like Questionnaire.item.option.value via Questionnaire Answer Codes.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 11208, preserved as git commit 8b49640a10f8413c2cc52e53e671632d034791c8 (#12442 - Questionnaire bindings), which added the historical QuestionnaireQuestionOption2 example binding to questionnaire-spreadsheet.xml. Later source refactoring moved the authoritative definition into source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. The current source binds Questionnaire.item.enableWhen.answer[x], Questionnaire.item.answerOption.value[x], and the current wrapper form Questionnaire.item.initial.value[x] by example to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/questionnaire-answers. That value set composes from SNOMED CT, matching the Jira resolution direction. FHIR-13057 is related binding-presentation history but does not reverse the requested semantic binding coverage. Quoted Jira searches found only the seed for this missing-binding request; Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting direction.
reconciliation: No source edit was made because the active current build source already satisfies FHIR-12442. An empty no-change audit commit was published on the combined branch.
